feedback.finish: This is Julius Caesar, one of Rome’s most famous leaders. In 55 BC, his army invaded Britain.

atoms.b: Caesar brought 12,000 troops to Britain, but the Britons were waiting for him on the ((++beach boat)). The Romans had to fight just to land, and progress was slow.
The Romans also weren’t prepared for the bad weather. Storms meant that many of Caesar’s ((++ships shoes)), which were meant to bring more soldiers and food, wrecked before they could land.

instruction.text: Read what Caesar observed during the invasion attempt and complete the sentence.

atoms.finishSound: They rode chariots to create terror and confusion.

feedback.finish: Caesar and the Romans left Britain after only a few battles. However, he returned the very next year.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: For his second invasion, Caesar brought 50,000 soldiers and progressed all the way from the Kent coast to the River Thames.
The Britons and the Romans fought very differently. The Britons threw weapons from chariots and rode horses ferociously.
This worked very well against less organised enemies, but the Romans fought in strong formations and stopped the chariots from flanking them.

hint.label: Flanking
hint.text: Flanking means to attack the sides of an army, where they are less able to defend themselves.

atoms.a: How many soldiers did Caesar bring for his second invasion?
What strategy helped the Romans to victory?

feedback.finish: The Romans were stronger than the Britons, but before Caesar could make much progress, problems in Gaul forced him back to mainland Europe. He never came back to Britain.
